data.name: Methodology_Subtitle
data.value: A four-step methodology that turns own-source revenue data into a concrete reform plan. Each screenshot below is from the Nairobi sample report.

data.name: Methodology_Step1_Alt
data.value: Step 1 Gap Analysis dashboard showing the property tax matrix and revenue vs potential breakdown

data.name: Methodology_Step1_Body
data.value: For each revenue stream, the city enters only the inputs in the gray-shaded cells — registered units, billed amount, outstanding amount, statutory benchmark — and ROSRA decomposes the gap between current collection and full potential into specific drivers: Compliance, Coverage, Valuation or Liability, and the mixed gaps that combine them. The matrix dashboard on the right makes it instantly visible where each shilling is slipping through. Streams that don't apply to your context (e.g. Solid Waste Fee here) can be excluded.

data.name: Methodology_Step2_Alt
data.value: Step 2 Stream Prioritization table showing each revenue stream ranked by total functional gap

data.name: Methodology_Step2_Body
data.value: Streams are ranked by their Total Functional Gap and broken down per gap-type — Compliance, Coverage, Valuation/Liability, and the mixed gaps — in a single stacked bar so the city can see at a glance which reforms move the most revenue. Decision-makers can re-order, exclude, or remove specific gap-types that aren't politically feasible. Excluded streams (like Solid Waste Fee here) are dropped from rank, share, the bar chart, and the downstream Recommendations — the plan respects local realities, not just the math.

data.name: Methodology_Step3_Alt
data.value: Step 3 Overview Selection — solution cards with implementation guidance

data.name: Methodology_Step3_Body
data.value: From a curated library of 82 evidence-based solution cards, ROSRA narrows the list by stream, gap-type, timeline, and political feasibility — and a 3-question personaliser tailors them to the city's context. Each card explains what the option does, most useful when, usually not the best first move when, and often works best alongside. The right-hand Selection Summary tracks every pick by stream and gap, with a one-click jump straight to Recommendations once you have enough.

data.name: Methodology_Step4_Alt
data.value: Step 4 Recommendations — consolidated action plan with timelines and quick-win tags

data.name: Methodology_Step4_Body
data.value: The selected solutions are consolidated into a single implementation plan, grouped by stream and ranked by priority, with each card timeline-tagged as a Quick Win (<1 year), Medium Term (1–3 years), or Long Term (3+ years). Switch between Solution Cards, Timeline View, and Progress Tracker views — then export the whole plan to PDF or HTML as the city's tailored Revenue Enhancement Action Plan.
